findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Annual Report 2025-26
findings.headline: General fund financing costs improved dramatically to 25.2% of net revenue stream from 43.8%
findings.detail: General fund financing costs as a proportion of net revenue stream have roughly halved, falling from 43.8% to 25.2%. This substantial improvement reflects the combined impact of lower borrowing levels, debt repayment, and MRP management adjustments.
findings.matters: Indicates significant improvement in the council's debt servicing capacity and overall financial flexibility; a major positive indicator for lenders assessing creditworthiness.
findings.quote: The proportion of general fund financing costs to net revenue stream has reduced from 43.8% last year to 25.2%.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Annual Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Repaid £25m PWLB debt in October 2025, securing £12.9m discount saving
findings.detail: The council repaid ten PWLB loans totalling £25m in October 2025, achieving a discount saving of £12.9m that is being spread over 10 years for regulatory purposes. This generated £1.49m in annual financing cost savings (£1.29m discount plus £0.20m interest saving) in 2025/26.
findings.matters: Demonstrates active, skilled management of debt position and ability to take advantage of market opportunities; reduces future financing costs and improves financial flexibility.
findings.figures: £25m repaid; £12.9m discount saving; £1.49m annual financing cost saving
findings.quote: Ten PWLB loans with a face value of £25m were repaid on 29/10/25, with a discount saving of £12.9m (spread over 10 years) so that only £12.1m was repayable.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Annual Report 2025-26
findings.headline: £28.3m loaned to subsidiary companies with modest interest returns of £1.3m
findings.detail: The council has extended £28.3m in loans to three subsidiary entities: Eastbourne Housing Investment Company Limited, South East Environmental Services Limited, and Aspiration Homes LLP joint venture. Interest received on these loans is £1.3m, representing a 4.6% return.
findings.matters: This represents material council exposure to subsidiary company performance; if subsidiaries underperform or default, the council loses both principal and interest income, affecting overall financial position.
findings.quote: As at 31 March 2026, a total of £28.3m loans have been provided and the interest received on those loans was £1.3m.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Annual Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Housing Revenue Account financing costs rising to 31.1% of rental income from 27.7%
findings.detail: HRA financing costs have increased from 27.7% to 31.1% of rental income, tightening the HRA's financial flexibility. The council attributes this increase to higher depreciation charges.
findings.matters: Lenders monitor HRA headroom; rising financing cost ratios reduce the HRA's ability to invest in repairs, improvements, or to absorb volatility in rental income.
findings.quote: The proportion of HRA financing costs to rental income was 31.1% compared to 27.7% last year, the increase due to higher depreciation.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Annual Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Capital programme delivered at only 72% of budget with significantly lower borrowing requirement
findings.detail: Capital expenditure was £31.9m against a budgeted £44m, and the borrowing requirement was £7.4m against an estimated £25m. The programme was materially underspent, particularly in HRA (£17.0m actual vs £32.6m budgeted).
findings.matters: Lenders need to assess whether capital plans are being delivered on schedule; significant variance suggests either delayed projects, scope reduction, or delivery constraints that could affect future capital investment capacity.
findings.quote: The actual capital outturn for the year was lower at £31.9m (GF £14.9m and HRA £17.0m), with a total borrowing need of £7.4m (GF £3.3m and HRA £4.1m).

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Annual Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Commercial and service investment income fell sharply to 7.6% of net revenue stream from 12.4%
findings.detail: The council's net income from commercial and service investments as a proportion of net revenue stream has declined significantly, from 12.4% to 7.6%. This represents a material reduction in returns on commercial activity that the council depends on for revenue.
findings.matters: A lender or finance director needs to understand the sustainability of the council's commercial income base; declining returns suggest either underperforming assets or reduced investment volumes, which affects overall financial flexibility.
findings.quote: The proportion of net income from commercial and service investments to net revenue stream has reduced from 12.4% last year to 7.6%.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: Revenue and Capital Financial Outturn 2025-26 final
findings.headline: HRA incurred £267k in disrepair compensation and legal costs, indicating tenant complaints and regulatory risk
findings.detail: In addition to routine repairs costs, the HRA incurred £267k in disrepair compensation claims and legal costs during the year. The council acknowledges these represent reactive responses to tenant complaints and states that earlier intervention is expected to reduce future costs. The council is also engaging with government on claims management practices.
findings.matters: Rising disrepair claims suggest reactive rather than preventative maintenance approach; regulatory risk given RSH oversight and tenant protection standards; legal exposure from claims management activity.
findings.figures: Disrepair and legal costs £267k; overdue repairs brought down to 3.38% of 15,011 work orders
findings.quote: The service also incurred an additional £267k in disrepair compensation and legal costs. Earlier intervention and more effective management of cases through appropriate legal routes is expected to reduce future costs.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: Revenue and Capital Financial Outturn 2025-26 final
findings.headline: General Fund balance achieved through in-year mitigations and central contingencies, not structural base budget delivery
findings.detail: The General Fund outturn is balanced overall, but this reflects the combined effect of service pressures, delivery of savings, and careful use of centrally controlled budgets and corporate mitigations. While 98% of the savings programme was delivered, the report explicitly notes that reliance on in-year mitigations presents medium-term risks. Recurring service pressures in Corporate Services, Tourism and Place, and Temporary Accommodation persist.
findings.matters: Balance achieved through contingencies rather than base budget control suggests structural imbalance; future mitigation options are limited and recurring pressures threaten medium-term sustainability.
findings.quote: This reflects the combined effect of service pressures, delivery of savings, and careful use of centrally controlled budgets and corporate mitigations.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: Revenue and Capital Financial Outturn 2025-26 final
findings.headline: Capital programme underspent by £5.66m with only 85% delivered, indicating forecast and delivery challenges
findings.detail: Total capital expenditure was £31.91m against a revised budget of £37.57m, a shortfall of £5.66m (-15.1%). General Fund capital was £14.98m against £18.30m budget (-18.1%); HRA capital was £16.93m against £19.27m budget (-12.1%). Key delays occurred in regeneration schemes (Victoria Place, Black Robin Farm) where market conditions changed substantially, requiring design and pricing review. Slippage is expected to be carried forward into 2026-27.
findings.matters: Underspend reduces service improvement and regeneration outcomes; Black Robin Farm design/pricing review suggests viability risk; programme delivery challenges indicate risk of future overspends or extended timelines.
findings.figures: Total underspend £5.66m (-15.1%); GF underspend £3.32m (-18.1%); HRA underspend £2.33m (-12.1%); Regeneration underspend £1.18m; New Build underspend £2.58m
findings.quote: The scale of the variance points to challenges in programme delivery, forecasting and phasing, with expenditure shifting into future years rather than being removed.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: Revenue and Capital Financial Outturn 2025-26 final
findings.headline: Emergency and temporary accommodation remains the largest pressure facing the council, with demand declining but still elevated
findings.detail: Household numbers in temporary accommodation peaked at 257 in Q1, remained at 253 in Q2, but were brought down to 238 by Q3 and 214 by year-end through sustained management and prevention work. Despite slower-than-planned reduction and high costs, the service achieved a small £185k underspend. The council acknowledges ongoing affordability challenges and the need for longer-term solutions including increased supply.
findings.matters: This is identified as the largest and most disproportionate pressure the council faces; demand-led costs create budget volatility and ongoing affordability challenges signal structural housing market issues affecting the council's area.
findings.quote: Emergency and temporary accommodation remains the largest and most disproportionate pressure faced by the Council, reflecting both increased demand and the high cost of provision.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: Revenue and Capital Financial Outturn 2025-26 final
findings.headline: Housing Revenue Account overspent by £332k against revised net budget despite management action
findings.detail: The HRA experienced an overspend of £332k against a revised net budget of £141k. This was driven by £780k additional repairs and maintenance costs (largely one-off effort to clear COVID-related backlog), £267k in disrepair compensation and legal costs, and a £631k increase in depreciation charges from updated property valuations. Mitigations included staff vacancies (£207k), reduced heating costs (£91k), capitalised transformation costs (£267k), and utility savings (£51k).
findings.matters: HRA is ring-fenced and overspends constrain future capital investment in housing and must be recovered from reserves or future budgets; rising repairs and legal costs suggest maintenance backlog and tenant complaint issues.
findings.figures: Overspend £332k; repairs costs £780k; disrepair/legal costs £267k; depreciation increase £631k; Major Works budget exceeded by £493k
findings.quote: The Housing Revenue Account has closed the year with an overspend of £332,000 against the revised net budget, reflecting the challenging financial and changing regulatory environment, with inflationary and legal cost pressures continuing throughout the year in addition to an intensified focus on the repairs service.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Eastbourne Quarterly report on Audit and Counter Fraud work
findings.headline: Several audit-identified control weaknesses remain outstanding after multiple follow-up reviews
findings.detail: Multiple audit areas have been through repeated follow-up cycles with recommendations still unresolved: Risk Management (4th follow-up), Complaints (5th follow-up), and Casual Workers (3rd follow-up with four recommendations still outstanding). This indicates slow or incomplete implementation of audit-identified improvements.
findings.matters: Repeated follow-ups without closure suggest weak implementation capacity for audit recommendations. This means identified control gaps remain unaddressed for extended periods, increasing organisational risk.
findings.figures: Risk Management 4th follow-up, Complaints 5th follow-up, Casual Workers 3rd follow-up
findings.quote: Casual Workers (3rd follow up) Action against one recommendation is in progress with four others outstanding.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Eastbourne Quarterly report on Audit and Counter Fraud work
findings.headline: Audit team staffing losses delayed verification that prior-year audit recommendations were implemented
findings.detail: The audit team lost two staff at end of November plus another during the year, leaving the function understaffed until new recruits joined in mid-April. This caused delays in follow-up reviews that verify whether management has implemented audit recommendations, meaning the council could not confirm its control environment was properly functioning for several months.
findings.matters: Audit follow-ups verify that control weaknesses are actually being fixed. Delays in follow-ups mean the council cannot confirm its control environment is improving, creating a gap in governance oversight.
findings.figures: Two auditors departed end November, another during year; new staff joined 13 April
findings.quote: It should be noted that some follow ups have been delayed due to the limited staffing in the Audit team during this period. Therefore, it is possible that more recommendations have been addressed but that the follow up has not yet taken place.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: EBC Audit and Governance Annual Report 2025-26 - FINAL 12.6.26
findings.headline: Committee self-assessment reveals governance gaps in oversight of major projects, arms-length companies, and financial reporting during a period of organizational upheaval from Local Government Reorganisation
findings.detail: The committee identifies that its Terms of Reference do not explicitly address value for money, financial reporting arrangements, or internal audit independence. Simultaneously, the council faces significant organizational risk from potential Local Government Reorganisation (LGR), which the committee recognises will create 'governance, risk and control challenges'.
findings.matters: Weak oversight frameworks during periods of organizational instability increase exposure to financial loss, poor decision-making, and ineffective risk management in major projects and subsidiary entities.
findings.quote: The Committee recognises the potential governance, risk and control challenges arising from Local Government Reorganisation, in addition to existing 'business as usual' pressures.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: EBC Audit and Governance Annual Report 2025-26 - FINAL 12.6.26
findings.headline: External auditor identified Value for Money concerns in 2024-25 that the committee must now substantively review and integrate into governance arrangements
findings.detail: The committee's forward agenda includes a requirement to undertake 'further consideration of the substantive findings and recommendations arising from the External Auditor's Value for Money work for 2024 to 2025'. The paper does not detail what those findings are, but their existence is flagged as requiring action.
findings.matters: External auditor VFM findings indicate the council is not deploying resources effectively or achieving planned outcomes; these must be understood to assess financial sustainability and management capability.
findings.quote: Review Value for Money Findings and Assurance Recommendations arising from the External Auditor's Value for Money work for 2024 to 2025, including how these are reflected within the Council's governance and improvement arrangements.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: EBC Audit and Governance Annual Report 2025-26 - FINAL 12.6.26
findings.headline: External auditors identified that there is no formal escalation process for departments to explain or revise overdue internal audit recommendations
findings.detail: The audit and governance committee has had to petition the Corporate Management Team to encourage managers to address outstanding audit recommendations. The external auditors explicitly flagged the absence of a formal process requiring written explanations and revised timelines when recommendations are not completed on schedule.
findings.matters: Failure to implement internal audit recommendations indicates management weakness and control gaps; the absence of a formal escalation process means overdue risks are not being systematically addressed.
findings.quote: We have particularly noted the external auditors' observation that there is no formal escalation process for departments to provide written explanations and revised timelines for overdue internal audit recommendations.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: EBC Audit and Governance Annual Report 2025-26 - FINAL 12.6.26
findings.headline: Aged debt management has been a significant control weakness requiring continuing monitoring through 2026-27
findings.detail: The committee specifically requested reports on debt management improvements and monitored progress on audit recommendations. By February 2026, the council's Assistant Director confirmed all planned process improvements were in place. However, the committee explicitly notes that 'the full impact will continue to be monitored during 2026 to 2027'—indicating uncertainty about whether the fix has actually resolved the problem.
findings.matters: Aged debt indicates weak receivables control and cash collection processes, affecting cash flow, financial forecasting, and the council's ability to meet obligations.
findings.quote: In some areas, including debt management and implementation of audit recommendations, early indications of improvement have been observed, although the full impact will continue to be monitored during 2026 to 2027.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Strategic Risk Register Quarterly Review
findings.headline: UK Terrorism Threat Level raised to Severe by COBR, increasing civil contingencies risk likelihood
findings.detail: Following COBR's escalation of the UK Terrorism Threat Level to Severe, the council increased the likelihood component of its Civil Contingencies Act risk from Possible to Likely. New monitoring controls were added to track COBR threat level changes and maintain liaison with Sussex Resilience Forum.
findings.matters: Terrorist incidents could disrupt council operations and service continuity; threat level escalation increases the assessed likelihood of disruption affecting service delivery and revenue.
findings.quote: The Terrorism Threat Level issued by COBR had been raised to Severe (an attack is highly likely)

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Strategic Risk Register Quarterly Review
findings.headline: Eastbourne has eliminated reliance on Exceptional Financial Support and paid off associated borrowing, reducing financial risk from Red to Amber
findings.detail: The Director of Performance and Finance confirmed that with a balanced Medium Term Financial Strategy, the council has successfully eliminated its reliance on Exceptional Financial Support and paid off all associated borrowing. This achievement prompted a downgrade of the council's economic environment risk from Red to Amber, with likelihood reduced from Highly Likely to Likely and impact reduced from Critical to Major.
findings.matters: Lenders closely monitor whether councils have resolved structural budget deficits and dependency on exceptional support; elimination of reliance on EFS signals transition from vulnerability to financial stability.
findings.figures: Risk level: Red to Amber; Likelihood: 4 (Highly Likely) to 3 (Likely); Impact: 5 (Critical) to 4 (Major)
findings.quote: with the balanced Medium Term Financial Strategy and the successful elimination of reliance on Exceptional Financial Support, as well as paying off all the associated borrowing, the risk scores could be reduced

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: 2. EBC External Audit Recommendaions - Update
findings.headline: Council will measure only the top 10 highest-value properties at £20k cost rather than full £300-325k remediation of asset valuation evidence
findings.detail: Three options were evaluated: do nothing, measure all properties (£300-325k cost), or measure high-value properties only (£20k). The council selected the phased approach to measure approximately the top 10 properties. This is intended to reduce audit risk from medium to low but represents a partial fix.
findings.matters: The partial remediation shows responsiveness to audit concerns but means full asset valuation risk remains unresolved. Lenders should note this is not a complete fix to a material control weakness.
findings.quote: Option 3 was the preferred approach, which proposes measuring a limited number of high-value properties (e.g., the top 10 per council) at an estimated cost of £20k. This would demonstrate progress, potentially reduce audit risk from medium to low, and support improved valuation evidence for future accounts.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: 2. EBC External Audit Recommendaions - Update
findings.headline: Nearly 30% of the council's £445m asset base (£129m) lacks documented supporting evidence for floor plan-based valuations
findings.detail: Around £129m of the council's £445m asset value depends on floor area or site area-based valuation methods but lacks supporting floor plan documentation. Supporting evidence is often missing, reducing audit confidence. Auditors recommend establishing a central indexed repository of floor plans and corresponding GIA data.
findings.matters: Without documented supporting evidence for nearly a third of reported assets, the balance sheet's reliability is compromised. This directly concerns lenders about the accuracy of the council's financial position.
findings.quote: Of the total £445m asset value in Eastbourne, around £129m (29%) falls within scope for this issue, as it depends on floor/site area-based valuation methods. While some historic floor area data exists, supporting evidence is often lacking, reducing audit confidence.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: 2. EBC External Audit Recommendaions - Update
findings.headline: Grant Thornton will disclaim the audit opinion for 2025/26, citing cumulative historic issues and audit evidence limitations
findings.detail: Auditors have already confirmed the 2025/26 opinion will be disclaimed. This is attributed to cumulative impact of historic issues and limitations on obtaining sufficient appropriate audit evidence, not just current-year performance. A disclaimed opinion means auditors cannot verify the accounts are materially correct.
findings.matters: A disclaimed audit opinion signals to lenders that auditors could not obtain sufficient evidence to sign off on the accounts. This undermines confidence in the council's financial reporting and control environment.
findings.quote: Grant Thornton (GT) has already confirmed that the audit opinion for 2025/26 will continue to be disclaimed. This reflects the cumulative impact of historic issues and the limitations placed on the auditors' ability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Apppendix 2 - Strategic Risk Register
findings.headline: Aged debt is trending upwards as low-income households struggle with economic pressure
findings.detail: The register notes that the aged debt trend reflects wider economic pressures on low-income households, indicating the council's ability to collect revenue is deteriorating as residents' incomes weaken.
findings.matters: Rising aged debt signals deteriorating council tax and other income collection at a time when the council is already squeezed by inflation and rising demand
findings.quote: The aged debt trend reflects the wider economic pressures on low income households

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Apppendix 2 - Strategic Risk Register
findings.headline: Homelessness presentations are increasing and will drain the General Fund while housing benefit subsidy income is reducing
findings.detail: The register identifies increased homelessness due to economic pressures, lack of social housing, and rising private rents. It explicitly states the nightly paid accommodation budget will be impacted, and that the loss of Housing Benefit Subsidy will increase at year-end — meaning the council receives less subsidy to cover these costs.
findings.matters: This is a demand-driven, unfunded pressure: the council must house more people while receiving less grant support, directly draining reserves and general fund
findings.quote: Increased homelessness presentations due to the economic situation, lack of available social housing and rising private sector rents leads to an increased number that require prevention or place into emergency accommodation. This will have a detrimental impact on the resource required for prevention and the General Fund. The nightly paid accommodation budget will be impacted and, more significantly, the loss of Housing Benefit Subsidy will increase at the end of the financial year.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Apppendix 2 - Strategic Risk Register
findings.headline: Inflation is currently having a serious impact on the council's finances
findings.detail: The risk register explicitly identifies residual inflation as a current pressure affecting council costs. It is listed as one of the active impacts on the council's finances, alongside rising energy prices that are affecting both the council's operations and residents' ability to pay.
findings.matters: A lender must know whether the council can manage cost growth; this statement confirms inflation is actively eroding the financial position now, not potentially in future
findings.quote: Residual inflation affecting council costs is having a serious impact on the council's finances.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - 2025-26 Eastbourne Annual Governance Statement
findings.headline: CIPFA Assurance Review identified multiple improvement areas requiring remedial action by the council
findings.detail: A CIPFA Assurance Review in summer 2025 identified multiple areas where improvements were needed, leading to establishment of a Strategic Finance Board, review of risk management policy, economic development strategy, procurement function review, and enhanced monitoring of borrowing costs.
findings.matters: An external professional assessment by CIPFA identified gaps in the council's financial management and governance frameworks, indicating that the council does not yet meet the standards that leading local authorities achieve.
findings.quote: Following the CIPFA Assurance Review undertaken in the summer of 2025 the Council has taken the opportunity to act on several areas where improvements have been suggested by CIPFA

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - 2025-26 Eastbourne Annual Governance Statement
findings.headline: Risk management remains not fully embedded across the organisation despite improvements during the year
findings.detail: The Chief Internal Auditor notes that risk management has historically not been embedded across the council and while there has been improvement (department-level risk registers established), more work remains necessary.
findings.matters: Incomplete risk management embedding means not all services are consistently identifying, documenting, and escalating risks, reducing the council's ability to anticipate and respond to emerging financial or operational threats.
findings.quote: Previously the opinion has been caveated by the issues of risk management not being embedded across the organisation and the number of recommendations made by Internal Audit that have not been addressed. However, during this financial year action has been taken on outstanding recommendations and risk registers are now held for each department. More work is necessary but there has been a general improvement.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - 2025-26 Eastbourne Annual Governance Statement
findings.headline: Internal audit function was understaffed in Q4 2025-26 after losing staff, creating a control assurance gap
findings.detail: The Internal Audit team lost staff at the end of Q3 and was operating understaffed for the full final quarter until a recruitment exercise could fill the posts. The Chief Internal Auditor concluded that sufficient work was completed despite this gap.
findings.matters: Understaffing in internal audit during the final quarter of the financial year means the full population of transactions and controls may not have been adequately tested or monitored, reducing the reliability of year-end financial assurance.
findings.figures: One quarter of the year affected (Q4 2025-26)
findings.quote: The Internal Audit team lost staff at the end of the third quarter of the year and was therefore understaffed in the final quarter of the year, until a recruitment exercise could be undertaken.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - 2025-26 Eastbourne Annual Governance Statement
findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation will dissolve Eastbourne Borough Council and absorb it into a unitary authority by 2028, creating governance uncertainty
findings.detail: The council is actively preparing for potential dissolution and absorption into a unitary authority across East Sussex, with a final decision expected in summer 2026 and implementation by 2028. The council is already experiencing risk of staff retention and expects additional officer capacity pressure during the transition.
findings.matters: Organisational dissolution creates uncertainty about service continuity, asset allocation, and staff retention. The council explicitly flagged staff retention as a risk and anticipated capacity constraints managing both business-as-usual and transition activities.
findings.figures: Reorganisation expected 2028; final decision pending summer 2026
findings.quote: The Council remains committed to advocating for the best outcomes for its residents and stakeholders in any future local government configuration.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - 2025-26 Eastbourne Annual Governance Statement
findings.headline: Council is principal guarantor of a £48m refinancing loan on a private property in Leicester via subsidiary Investment Company Eastbourne
findings.detail: The council's wholly-owned company ICE has committed the council as ultimate guarantor on a £48m refinancing loan to a private company holding a property in Leicester. The council controls 49.5% of ordinary shares by option but does not currently hold a majority shareholding.
findings.matters: The £48m guarantee is a contingent liability that could crystallise if the private company defaults or if returns fall short of the business plan. This exposure is material relative to a small council's borrowing capacity.
findings.figures: £48m refinancing loan; council holds up to 49.5% of shares by option
findings.quote: ICE is acting as the principal guarantor of a £48m refinancing loan to a private company, with Eastbourne Borough Council being the ultimate guarantor.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - 2025-26 Eastbourne Annual Governance Statement
findings.headline: Council delivered only 93% of planned savings and efficiencies in the year of exiting Exceptional Financial Support
findings.detail: The council exited Exceptional Financial Support (EFS) arrangements in the prior year but achieved only 93% of planned savings in 2025-26, meaning a 7% shortfall against the transformation programme it is relying on to prevent a return to financial distress.
findings.matters: Missing savings targets by 7% in the year of EFS exit signals the council is not delivering the financial stabilisation it is dependent on. This increases the risk of return to EFS or mounting deficits if target-setting is optimistic.
findings.figures: 93% delivery rate (7% shortfall on planned savings and efficiencies)
findings.quote: delivering 93% of our planned savings and efficiencies this year—a critical step in exiting our reliance on Exceptional Financial Support (EFS) arrangements.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - 2025-26 Eastbourne Annual Governance Statement
findings.headline: Homelessness and temporary accommodation is an ongoing cost pressure compounded by interest rates and business rates volatility
findings.detail: The council identifies high levels of homelessness and temporary accommodation placements as an ongoing cost driver, explicitly compounded by high interest rates, volatility in business rates income, and inflationary pressures. This multi-factor pressure is severe enough that the council created a Strategic Finance Programme specifically to manage it.
findings.matters: Homelessness and temporary accommodation are structural cost pressures that grow outside the council's control and directly impact the ability to balance budgets. Business rates volatility and interest rate sensitivity are material revenue risks for a lender to assess.
findings.figures: No specific figures provided on cost of homelessness/temp accommodation, but identified as primary driver of Strategic Finance Programme
findings.quote: Eastbourne Borough Council continues to tackle high levels of homelessness and temporary accommodation placements. This ongoing cost pressure is compounded by high interest rates, volatility in business rates income and inflationary pressures.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Full Council
findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Section 25 Statement of S151 Officer
findings.headline: Continued uncertainty regarding business rates retention and government funding adjustments requires ongoing tight financial control
findings.detail: The CFO identifies ongoing risks from business rates retention uncertainty, adjustments in government funding, and external economic or legislative influences. The council must continue to implement savings and efficiency strategies each year and maintain tight financial control to navigate these risks.
findings.matters: External funding volatility could undermine budget assumptions and force additional savings delivery at short notice, testing the council's financial flexibility
findings.quote: However, there remains continued uncertainty regarding business rates retention, adjustments in government funding, and other external economic or legislative influences. To address these risks, the Council must continue to implement its savings and efficiency strategies each year.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Full Council
findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Section 25 Statement of S151 Officer
findings.headline: Strategic Financial Programme has achieved almost £7m in savings with forecast to exceed £8m by end of 2026/27
findings.detail: The savings programme has been critical to restoring financial health. It has delivered almost £7m to date and is forecast to achieve more than £8m by the end of 2026/27. The 2026/27 balanced budget depends on continued delivery of this programme.
findings.matters: The council's balanced budget position is contingent on achieving this ambitious savings target; any shortfall would immediately create a deficit
findings.figures: £7m achieved to date, £8m+ forecast by end 2026/27
findings.quote: our successful Strategic Financial Programme has currently achieved almost £7m and is forecast to achieve more than £8m of savings and efficiencies by the end of 2026/27

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Full Council
findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Section 25 Statement of S151 Officer
findings.headline: Housing Revenue Account future projections warrant review due to uncertainties in rent policies, inflation, and business plan sustainability
findings.detail: While the HRA has a balanced budget for 2026/27 with general reserves at £2.2m, the CFO identifies that future projections need review because of risks from rental policy changes and inflation, and explicitly recommends close monitoring and proactive adjustments to the HRA business plan.
findings.matters: The HRA is a material part of council operations; sustainability challenges here could cascade to affect overall council financial stability
findings.quote: However, future projections warrant review due to uncertainties in rent policies, inflation, and the sustainability of the HRA business plan. Close monitoring and proactive adjustments to the business plan are recommended.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Full Council
findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Section 25 Statement of S151 Officer
findings.headline: 2026/27 reserves of £2.575m meet the minimum requirement but fall short of the optimal £4m level
findings.detail: The CFO recommends maintaining at least £2.5m in unallocated General Fund reserves, aiming for optimal £4m, with a maximum of £5m. The forecasted level of £2.575m barely exceeds the minimum threshold, providing minimal buffer above the safety floor.
findings.matters: Limited reserves mean the council has minimal headroom for unexpected costs or revenue shortfalls, increasing vulnerability to shocks
findings.quote: The forecasted reserve for 2026/27 is £2.575m, which meets the minimum requirement but does not reach the optimal level, underscoring the need for careful stewardship.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Full Council
findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Section 25 Statement of S151 Officer
findings.headline: Eastbourne will exit Exceptional Financial Support at the end of 2025/26, a year earlier than planned
findings.detail: After several years requiring exceptional financial support following COVID and the housing crisis, the council has now paid back that support and will exit a year ahead of schedule. This marks the beginning of a recovery phase and the council now can begin to rebuild financial resilience.
findings.matters: Shows the council has recently emerged from acute financial distress and dependency on government support, important context for credit assessment
findings.figures: Exiting end of 2025/26, one year early
findings.quote: we will exit (and have paid back) Exceptional Financial Support at the end of 2025/26, a year earlier than planned

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix A - EBC Audit Findings Report ISA 260 for 2024-25
findings.headline: Pension fund data variances and prior-year assurance gap create uncertainty over pension liability valuation
findings.detail: The pension fund auditor identified a non-trivial variance of £313k in contributions received, a projected misstatement of £3.1m in benefits paid (prorated £125k to council), and a factual error of £8.18m in level 3 investment valuation (prorated £329k to council). However, since there is no assurance over the prior year pension liability, the auditor cannot conclude on accuracy of current year net liability valuation.
findings.matters: The pension liability (£2.267m) is sensitive to small changes in key assumptions. Data variances and errors in the fund, combined with no prior-year assurance, mean the council's reported liability cannot be independently verified.
findings.figures: pension liability £2.267m, contributions variance £313k, benefits variance £125k (prorated), investment error £329k (prorated)
findings.quote: we are unable to conclude on the accuracy of its net liabilities valuation for the current year as well because of the impact of no prior year audits.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix A - EBC Audit Findings Report ISA 260 for 2024-25
findings.headline: Investment property valuation differences not fully resolved; £14m post-year-end disposal not yet reflected
findings.detail: The auditor identified a £280k difference between the valuation report and the fixed asset register for investment properties. Post year-end, the council sold one investment property for £14m, which will be disclosed as a non-adjusting post balance sheet event rather than reflected in the accounts.
findings.matters: A £14m disposal of an investment property represents a significant capital transaction. If proceeds are not promptly reinvested or if there were planned reliance on this asset for cash flow, this represents a material change in financial position.
findings.quote: Post year end, the Council sold one of the investment property assets for £14m. This will be disclosed in the financial statements as a non adjusting post balance sheet event.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix A - EBC Audit Findings Report ISA 260 for 2024-25
findings.headline: Outstanding audit evidence prevents completion of testing across key financial statement areas
findings.detail: After selecting 502 audit samples with average response time of 2 weeks (range 1-55 days), the auditor was unable to complete testing across multiple areas due to time constraints imposed by the statutory backstop. Areas with incomplete testing include: financial instruments, related parties, assets disposal, assets under construction, creditors, debtors, and expected credit loss.
findings.matters: Incomplete audit procedures mean the auditor has not obtained assurance over significant areas of the financial statements. This prevents meaningful audit conclusions and indicates either inadequate records or serious process failures.
findings.figures: 502 samples selected, average response 2 weeks (target 3 days), range 1-55 days
findings.quote: These issues prevented us from completing our planned audit testing across key areas of the financial statements including financial instruments, related parties, assets disposal, assets under construction, creditors, debtors, expected credit loss.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix A - EBC Audit Findings Report ISA 260 for 2024-25
findings.headline: Segregation of duties weakness in journal posting and approval for journals under £100k
findings.detail: The auditor identified that the accounting system does not enforce segregation of duties between journal posters and approvers. While manual review occurs for journals over £100k, there remains a risk that journals below this threshold may lack proper segregation of duties. The auditor recommends: 'the Council should configure the financial system to prevent users from both posting and approving the same journal entry.'
findings.matters: Weak journal controls create fraud and error risk. An individual posting and approving their own journal could hide misstatements or embezzlement, particularly in amounts under £100k.
findings.quote: There remains a risk that journals below £100k may lack proper segregation of duties, increasing the likelihood of unauthorized or fraudulent journals going undetected. We recommend the Council should configure the financial system to prevent users from both posting and approving the same journal entry.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix A - EBC Audit Findings Report ISA 260 for 2024-25
findings.headline: Council unable to provide audit evidence for IFRS 16 lease compliance; auditor cannot conclude on implementation
findings.detail: The auditor requested a questionnaire on lease identification (14 April 2025) with no response received. A second request for list of all rental payments (17 October 2025) was also not provided. Without this information, the auditor states: 'we were unable to design and perform appropriate audit procedures. Consequently, we cannot conclude on the accuracy of the Council's assessment that the implementation of IFRS 16 had no material impact on its financial statements.'
findings.matters: IFRS 16 implementation (effective 1 April 2024) requires all leases to be recognised on-balance sheet. If not properly accounted for, this could materially misstate liabilities. The council's failure to provide basic information suggests inadequate processes.
findings.figures: questionnaire issued 14 April 2025 (no response), rental payment request 17 October 2025 (not provided)
findings.quote: we cannot conclude on the accuracy of the Council's assessment that the implementation of IFRS 16 had no material impact on its financial statements.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix A - EBC Audit Findings Report ISA 260 for 2024-25
findings.headline: Housing Benefits income cut-off error: prior year income recorded in 2024/25 exceeding 50% of performance materiality
findings.detail: Income relating to the prior financial year was recorded in 2024/25, primarily due to delays in posting migration journals following the Housing Benefits system change in 2022/23. This item represents more than 50% of audit performance materiality (£1.56m), and is reported as an unadjusted misstatement that the auditor cannot resolve.
findings.matters: A post-dated revenue recording error in a material amount indicates either poor controls or system issues that persisted from 2022/23. This represents unresolved accounting error that misstates both years' results.
findings.quote: For one item representing more than 50% of audit performance materiality, we identified a cut-off error. Income relating to the prior financial year was recorded in 2024/25, primarily due to delays in posting migration journals following the Housing Benefits system change in 2022/23. This has been reported as an unadjusted audit misstatement.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix A - EBC Audit Findings Report ISA 260 for 2024-25
findings.headline: Potential £2.7 million valuation error in general fund assets cannot be resolved due to time constraints
findings.detail: For two assets valued on a Depreciated Replacement Cost basis, the auditor could not successfully agree the outcome with the valuer, highlighting a potential valuation difference of £2.7 million. The valuer stated the obsolescence factor was determined by professional judgment, but the difference exceeds audit materiality (£2.4m). The auditor notes: 'Given that land and building valuation represents a significant risk area and the identified difference exceeds audit materiality, we consider it appropriate to report this matter as an uncertainty.'
findings.matters: A potential £2.7m error in a £410m asset base indicates either material valuation error or inadequate audit procedures. This exceeds the council's materiality threshold and creates uncertainty about asset values.
findings.figures: £2.7 million potential valuation difference, £410.243 million in 2024/25 land and buildings, materiality £2.4m
findings.quote: For two assets, we could not successfully agree the outcome of the approach adopted by the valuer highlighting a potential valuation difference of £2.7 million... Given that land and building valuation represents a significant risk area and the identified difference exceeds audit materiality, we consider it appropriate to report this matter as an uncertainty.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix A - EBC Audit Findings Report ISA 260 for 2024-25
findings.headline: £14.5 million of duplicated council dwellings in fixed assets register, overstating financial position
findings.detail: As part of land and buildings valuation testing, the auditor identified properties totalling £14.5m which had been duplicated in the fixed assets register, overstating the financial statements by this amount. This was identified in their testing but the underlying reconciliation issues were not fully resolved due to time constraints.
findings.matters: A £14.5m overstatement of assets represents a material error in the council's balance sheet. This directly misstates the council's net worth and borrowing capacity, both critical to lender assessment.
findings.figures: £14.5 million duplicated in fixed assets register
findings.quote: In respect of council dwellings valuation, we identified properties amounting to £14.5m which had been duplicated in the fixed assets register, overstating the financial statements by this amount.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix A - EBC Audit Findings Report ISA 260 for 2024-25
findings.headline: Finance team capacity insufficient to service both councils' audits simultaneously to meet November deadline
findings.detail: The finance team produced seven statements of accounts across Eastbourne and Lewes in 2025 with capacity issues affecting audit query responses. Average response time was 2 weeks (target 3 days), ranging from 1 to 55 days. The auditor recommends: 'Following the end of the 2024/25 audit, the Council should reassess if the capacity of the finance team is sufficient to service both Councils' audits simultaneously to meet a deadline of 30 November in future years.'
findings.matters: Insufficient finance team capacity creates risk of poor financial reporting quality, delayed accounts, and continued audit delays. This is a structural problem affecting both councils and threatens ability to meet statutory reporting deadlines.
findings.figures: average response time 2 weeks (target 3 days), range 1-55 days, 502 samples tested
findings.quote: Following the end of the 2024/25 audit, the Council should reassess if the capacity of the finance team is sufficient to service both Councils' audits simultaneously to meet a deadline of 30 November in future years.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix A - EBC Audit Findings Report ISA 260 for 2024-25
findings.headline: Six significant weaknesses identified in value for money arrangements for economy, efficiency and effectiveness
findings.detail: The auditor has identified 6 significant weaknesses in the council's arrangements for securing proper value for money. The auditor explicitly states: 'We have not been able to satisfy ourselves that the Council made proper arrangements for securing economy, efficiency and effectiveness in its use of resources in 2024/25.'
findings.matters: VFM weaknesses indicate the council is not managing its resources properly, which directly affects service quality, financial sustainability, and ability to deliver value to taxpayers and service users.
findings.quote: We have not been able to satisfy ourselves that the Council made proper arrangements for securing economy, efficiency and effectiveness in its use of resources in 2024/25.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Audit and Governance Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix A - EBC Audit Findings Report ISA 260 for 2024-25
findings.headline: Auditor will disclaim opinion on financial statements due to inability to assure opening balances
findings.detail: The auditor has been unable to complete sufficient work to support an unmodified audit opinion before the backstop date. Due to prior years' audits being disclaimed, there is no assurance over opening balances for 2024/25, making it impossible to form an opinion. The auditor states: 'Our anticipated financial statements audit report opinion will be a disclaimer of audit opinion.'
findings.matters: A disclaimed opinion means a lender has no independent verification that the financial statements give a true and fair view of the council's financial position. This is the most serious audit outcome and directly undermines confidence in reported financial position.
findings.quote: Owing to the challenges of undertaking an audit where the previous years' audits were subject to backstop-related disclaimed audit opinions, we have been unable to undertake sufficient work to support an unmodified audit opinion in advance of the backstop date of 27 February 2026.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: General Fund Revenue Budget 2026/27 and Capital Programme Report
findings.headline: Council is exploring shared services and local government reorganisation with unknown financial implications
findings.detail: Cabinet is recommending that the council, with Lewes District Council, explore shared services opportunities with other East Sussex councils, positioned as groundwork for potential Local Government Reorganisation. The financial implications of any such arrangements are stated to be unknown.
findings.matters: Creates medium-term uncertainty about the council's structure and cost base; shared services or LGR could materially change service delivery model, staffing costs, and financial sustainability
findings.quote: The financial implications related to the exploration of shared services opportunities with other East Sussex councils, are unknown at this point, however it is anticipated that any arrangements will be mutually beneficial to all partners and should result in savings and efficiencies for the Council.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: General Fund Revenue Budget 2026/27 and Capital Programme Report
findings.headline: Council holds £472k contingency for service pressures despite achieving balanced budget, suggesting underlying volatility
findings.detail: While the 2026/27 budget is balanced, the council has set aside £1.225m total contingency reserves, with £472k specifically for service demands and pressures. This is in addition to contingencies for pay awards (£553k) and contract inflation (£200k), indicating the council expects unpredictable service cost movements.
findings.matters: Suggests that underlying service pressures remain volatile despite the balanced position; the size of service-pressure contingency implies genuine uncertainty about demand control
findings.quote: Service Pressures £0.472m Contingency to support service demands and pressures

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: General Fund Revenue Budget 2026/27 and Capital Programme Report
findings.headline: Council explicitly identifies interest rate risk as a threat to its ability to finance capital spending
findings.detail: The Section 151 Officer has flagged that high interest rates could constrain the council's financial capacity to meet capital financing costs. This is listed as a key risk alongside economic downturn, cost inflation, and funding methodology changes.
findings.matters: Indicates the council's debt servicing affordability is rate-sensitive; if rates remain elevated, the council may need to cut capital investment, defer projects, or increase council tax further
findings.quote: The risk of interest rate remaining high and the corresponding impact on the Council's financial capacity to meet its capital financing.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: General Fund Revenue Budget 2026/27 and Capital Programme Report
findings.headline: Council will rely on external borrowing to finance £46m General Fund capital programme, assuming future market conditions permit
findings.detail: Given budgetary pressures, the council has assumed no revenue contributions to capital financing. The capital programme (2025/26-2028/29) will be largely funded by internal borrowing initially, with external borrowing assumed in future years. The revenue costs of this financing are included in budget projections.
findings.matters: Establishes a borrowing dependency for capital investment; lenders need to assess whether the council's revenue budget has capacity to service external debt if rates remain elevated
findings.figures: £46m General Fund capital programme; £147m HRA capital programme (2025/26-2028/29)
findings.quote: Given the budgetary pressures experienced from the Council no revenue contributions have been assumed to finance capital which is largely funded by internal borrowing and an assumption of external borrowing in future years when market conditions allow

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: General Fund Revenue Budget 2026/27 and Capital Programme Report
findings.headline: Temporary accommodation demand persists; government grant restructuring forces £31k budget adjustment to services
findings.detail: Cost-of-living crisis continues to drive demand for temporary accommodation, creating ongoing pressure on the council. The Homelessness Prevention Grant has been restructured, splitting temporary accommodation costs (51% of the grant) into the core Revenue Support Grant and moving prevention costs into a separate ringfenced grant. This split has required the council to make a £31k budget adjustment to services.
findings.matters: Shows the council faces demand-led pressures beyond its control; the grant restructuring reveals that while overall grant increased, the distribution change forces service reductions despite higher funding
findings.figures: £31k budget adjustment made; TA element of HPG calculated at 51%
findings.quote: These challenges have resulted in increased demand for temporary accommodation and have placed significant pressure on the Council's resources... the split between CSP and a new ringfenced grant means that a budget adjustment to services of £31k has been made.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Strategy, Investment Strategy, Capital Strategy and Prudential Indicators 2026/27 Report
findings.headline: Capital expenditure peak of £55.35m in 2026/27 represents significant delivery risk and funding commitment
findings.detail: The council plans capital spending of £55.35m in 2026/27 (general fund £21.6m, HRA £33.7m), reflecting major investment in housing, regeneration and service improvements. This spending level is constrained by CFR constraints and available financing.
findings.matters: A lender needs to assess whether the council has the delivery capacity, management bandwidth and sustained funding to execute this capital programme over the next three years.
findings.quote: capital expenditure is projected to reach a peak of £55.35m (GF£21.6m, HRA 33.7m) in 2026/27. This reflects significant investment in Housing, regeneration, and service improvements

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Strategy, Investment Strategy, Capital Strategy and Prudential Indicators 2026/27 Report
findings.headline: Capital Financing Requirement (CFR) rising to £217.4m in 2026/27 signals increased borrowing need ahead
findings.detail: The CFR—the underlying need to borrow for capital—is projected to rise to £217.4m in 2026/27, indicating the council's capital programme will require substantially more borrowing capacity in the medium term despite current debt reduction.
findings.matters: A lender needs to assess the medium-term borrowing trajectory and whether the council's funding sources and delivery capacity can sustain the rising capital ambitions.
findings.quote: A rise to £217.4 million in 2026/27 signals an increased investment programme.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Strategy, Investment Strategy, Capital Strategy and Prudential Indicators 2026/27 Report
findings.headline: Borrowing reduced by £42m in nine months to £142m by December 2025
findings.detail: The council's borrowing fell from £184m in March 2025 to £142m by December 2025—a material reduction. This represents active debt reduction but at a pace that may affect the council's liquidity position if sustained.
findings.matters: A lender needs to understand the debt trajectory and whether the council can maintain this reduction rate while funding capital plans without depleting reserves unsustainably.
findings.quote: The Council's borrowing as of December 2025 was £142m (March 2025 £184m).

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: Housing Revenue Account (HRA) Revenue Budget and Rent Setting 2026/27 and HRA Capital Programme 2024-29 Report
findings.headline: Service charge recovery moving toward full cost but tenants only partially insulated from gas inflation
findings.detail: The council is moving toward full cost recovery for service charges but is capping the pass-through of gas price increases at 80% of actual cost in 2026/27 (up from 60% in 2025/26) to manage tenant affordability. This means the council is absorbing 20% of gas cost increases. Full recovery is planned for 2027/28, suggesting further tenant cost exposure ahead.
findings.matters: A lender needs to track whether service charge increases are sustainable without triggering arrears or void growth. The phased approach to full recovery suggests the council recognizes affordability risk; if this approach fails, the HRA could face higher bad debt or lower occupancy.
findings.figures: Gas price cap at 80% actual cost in 2026/27 (from 60% in 2025/26); full recovery targeted 2027/28; average service charges range £6.81–£55.83 per week (HB-eligible) and £16.30–£44.24 (non-HB)
findings.quote: To maintain a balance of tenant affordability, the Council proposes a second-year cap of 80% of actual (personal use) gas prices. This cap is an increase from 60% applied in 2025/26 and aims to introduce full recovery in 2027/28.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: Housing Revenue Account (HRA) Revenue Budget and Rent Setting 2026/27 and HRA Capital Programme 2024-29 Report
findings.headline: Bad debt arrears of £1.27m are only 68% provisioned, leaving a material unprovisioned tail
findings.detail: The council holds a bad debt provision of £866,660 against total arrears of £1,269,870, providing for only 68.2% of the balance. The remaining £403k is not provisioned, representing a contingent liability. The council expects to increase the provision by a further £40k in 2026/27, suggesting growing pressure on collection.
findings.matters: Bad debt arrears directly reduce HRA revenue and signal tenant hardship or collection challenges. An unprovisioned tail of £400k is material relative to the working balance of £2.2m, and any deterioration in collection would pressure the already-tight reserve.
findings.figures: Total arrears £1,269,870; bad debt provision £866,660 (68.2%); unprovisioned element ~£403,210; 2026/27 provision increase £40,000
findings.quote: At 1 April 2025, the provision held totalled £866,660 providing for 68.2% of the arrears balance of £1,269,870.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: Housing Revenue Account (HRA) Revenue Budget and Rent Setting 2026/27 and HRA Capital Programme 2024-29 Report
findings.headline: Major works program falls short of long-term maintenance needs identified in the Stock Condition Survey
findings.detail: The council's five-year major works budget totals £29.589m, but the council explicitly states this is 'an affordable level of investment' that, 'although affordable and helping to maintain the stock, without additional levels of subsidy the sums fall short of works required long-term, as identified in the Stock Condition Survey.' This structural underfunding of maintenance creates long-term asset risk.
findings.matters: A lender needs to understand the council's future capital requirements and asset condition. Underfunded maintenance creates deferred liability and increases the risk of emergency spending or deterioration in housing quality.
findings.figures: Five-year major works budget £29.589m (£7.375m in 2026/27); funded mainly from Major Repairs Reserve (depreciation transfer)
findings.quote: This sum and all sums required over the next 30-years reflect an affordable level of investment which will allow the Councils housing stock to be appropriately maintained. However, although affordable and helping to maintain the stock, without additional levels of subsidy the sums fall short of works required long-term, as identified in the Stock Condition Survey.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: Housing Revenue Account (HRA) Revenue Budget and Rent Setting 2026/27 and HRA Capital Programme 2024-29 Report
findings.headline: Pending government rent policy change in January 2026 creates material budget uncertainty; council has secured emergency delegated authority
findings.detail: The council's 2026/27 budget is based on the prudent assumption of no rent convergence and no increased PWLB concessionary rates, but the government's final decision was not confirmed at the time of writing. The council has sought delegated authority from Cabinet to revise the 2026/27 budget immediately if the government announces rent convergence or PWLB changes in January 2026, showing that material adjustments may be needed.
findings.matters: A lender assessing Eastbourne's income stability needs to know that a material portion of the budget depends on government policy due in January 2026. Rent convergence could increase income significantly (the council noted it would apply to over 70% of stock) or could be constrained by affordability limits.
findings.figures: Budget prepared on assumption of no rent convergence; convergence would affect 70% of council stock; 2026/27 rental income increase £4.800m
findings.quote: At the time of writing and consulting on this report, the intentions of the Government are not confirmed, and the budget proposals have been prepared on the prudent assumption of no rent convergence or increased concessionary rate on borrowing.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: Housing Revenue Account (HRA) Revenue Budget and Rent Setting 2026/27 and HRA Capital Programme 2024-29 Report
findings.headline: HRA debt will increase materially from 2026/27 as the council borrows to fund acquisitions and new builds
findings.detail: The council's HRA debt is expected to increase from £53.536m by March 2026 to fund a capital programme totalling £147.946m over five years (2026/30), with new borrowing planned once capital financing from other sources is exhausted. The new build and acquisition programme alone is budgeted at £25.864m in 2026/27. Average debt per property is currently £15.0k.
findings.matters: Lenders need to monitor the council's debt trajectory and borrowing capacity, especially if interest rates do not fall as forecast or if rent policy constraints prevent income growth.
findings.figures: 2025/26 debt £53.536m increasing; 2026/27 new build and acquisition budget £25.864m; average debt per property £15.0k; five-year capital programme £147.946m (£114.927m new build/acquisition, £29.589m major works, £2.390m adaptations)
findings.quote: In the short term from 2026/27, debt levels will increase as the Council borrows more to fund property acquisitions and new builds.

findings.committee: Eastbourne Borough Council Cabinet
findings.paper_title: Housing Revenue Account (HRA) Revenue Budget and Rent Setting 2026/27 and HRA Capital Programme 2024-29 Report
findings.headline: Long-term HRA sustainability remains uncertain despite a balanced budget for 2026/27
findings.detail: The council acknowledges that while it has achieved a balanced HRA budget for 2026/27 with a projected working balance of £2.247m, the 30-Year Business Plan sustainability remains uncertain. The working balance sits only marginally above the minimum required (£2.151m), and the council states explicitly that the minimum is 'maintained in all years but not without constraints'. Government reform risks, particularly rent policy changes, compound this uncertainty.
findings.matters: A lender needs to understand the HRA's structural viability. A council maintaining only a minimum buffer despite surpluses signals limited financial resilience if assumptions change.
findings.figures: Minimum working balance £2.151m (£600 per dwelling); projected balance at 31 March 2027 £2.247m; current debt £51.699m increasing to £53.536m by 31 March 2026
findings.quote: Whilst a balanced business plan has been achieved, the projected HRA working balance sits marginally above that of the minimum working balance and the long-term sustainability of setting a balanced HRA remains uncertain.

news_drafts.headline: General fund financing costs improved dramatically to 25.2% of net revenue stream from 43.8%
news_drafts.lead: Indicates significant improvement in the council's debt servicing capacity and overall financial flexibility; a major positive indicator for lenders assessing creditworthiness.

news_drafts.headline: Repaid £25m PWLB debt in October 2025, securing £12.9m discount saving
news_drafts.lead: Demonstrates active, skilled management of debt position and ability to take advantage of market opportunities; reduces future financing costs and improves financial flexibility.

news_drafts.headline: £28.3m loaned to subsidiary companies with modest interest returns of £1.3m
news_drafts.lead: This represents material council exposure to subsidiary company performance; if subsidiaries underperform or default, the council loses both principal and interest income, affecting overall financial position.
